name: Multigres
tagline: Alpha-stage, Vitess-inspired sharding, pooling and HA layer for unmodified PostgreSQL, led by Supabase.
description: Multigres is an open-source project, sponsored by Supabase and led by Vitess co-creator Sugu Sougoumarane, that aims to do for PostgreSQL what Vitess did for MySQL. It runs unmodified Postgres behind a wire-compatible gateway (multigateway), per-instance connection pools (multipooler), a Raft-based orchestrator for primary election and failover (multiorch), backup tooling with pgBackRest and a Kubernetes operator. The goal is horizontal sharding, connection scaling and high availability without forking Postgres. The first open-source release, v0.1.0, shipped in May 2026 and is explicitly alpha. Watch it if you plan to outgrow a single Postgres primary, but do not run production on it yet.

pricing.notes: Free and open source; expected to power horizontal scaling on Supabase in the future.

scale.notes: Designed for sharding across many Postgres primaries; sharding is still under development in the alpha.

strengths: Runs stock PostgreSQL, so extensions and tooling keep working
Architecture and team carry over lessons from Vitess
Built-in connection pooling, failover orchestration and backups
Apache 2.0 with a Kubernetes operator from day one
weaknesses: Alpha software: APIs and behavior will change
Sharding features are incomplete in the first release
Operational model adds several new components around Postgres
useCases: Evaluating a future path to shard Postgres without leaving it
Postgres HA and pooling experiments on Kubernetes
Contributing to the next-generation Postgres scaling layer
notIdealFor: Small databases that fit on one server
